rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: A parsing attributed by Ibn al-Faras to al-Shafiʿi coordinates 59:9 with 59:8 and treats 59:10 as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: ونسبه ابن الفرس في ( أحكام القرآن ) إلى الشافعي

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is reported to hold that when fayʾ is land, the imam may choose its disposition; it need not go to the listed recipients of Banu Nadir’s fayʾ.
rows.anchor: ونسبه ابن الفرس في ( أحكام القرآن ) إلى الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Ibn ʿAshur’s preferred parsing, “They say, Our Lord, forgive us” is a circumstantial clause describing those who came after the first believers.
rows.anchor: وجملة { يقولون ربنا اغفر لنا } على التفسير المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on the ghayn, ghill means envy and hatred.
rows.anchor: والغل بكسر الغين : الحسد والبغض

words: وَلَا تَجْعَلْ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلًّا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later believers ask God to cleanse them of envy toward earlier believers for the latter’s companionship with the Prophet, emigration, or support.
rows.anchor: أن يطهر نفوسهم من الغل والحسد للمؤمنين السابقين على ما أعطوه من فضيلة صحبة النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguishes later believers by the merit of praying for the early believers, inwardly loving them, and having no hatred toward them.
rows.anchor: ما يكسبهم فضيلة ليست للمهاجرين والأنصار ، وهي فضيلة الدعاء لهم بالمغفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended believers inwardly keep what they ask God for and train themselves to be content with it.
rows.anchor: يضمرون ما يدعون الله به لهم في نفوسهم ويرضوا أنفسهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims are duty-bound to praise their predecessors, love the Emigrants and Helpers, and honor them.
rows.anchor: وقد دلت الآية على أن حقا على المسلمين أن يذكروا سلفهم بخير

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says one who hates any Companion or harbors resentment toward him has no right to the Muslims’ fayʾ; he cited this verse.
rows.anchor: قال مالك : من كان يبغض أحدا من أصحاب محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أو كان قلبه عليه غل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur reads the praised prayer as an entitlement condition: fayʾ is God’s gift, not spoils earned in combat, and recipients must love predecessors without envy.
rows.anchor: فإن الفيء عطية أعطاها الله تلك الأصناف ولم يكتسبوها بحق قتال ، فاشترط الله عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik’s rule allows ordinary or legally grounded resentment between individuals, such as the dispute of al-ʿAbbas and ʿAli before ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: إلا ما كان من شنآن بين شخصين لأسباب عادية أو شرعية مثل ما كان بين العباس وعلي حين تحاكما إلى عمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As another example of legally grounded conflict, ʿUmar imposed the slander penalty on Abu Bakra.
rows.anchor: ومثل إقامة عمر حد القذف على أبي بكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following al-Muʾmin with al-Muhaymin prevents readers from mistaking God’s protection for weakness or fear; it is wise mercy from an all-seeing Lord.
rows.anchor: وتعقيب { المؤمن } ب { المهيمن } لدفع توهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAziz is unconquered and cannot be humiliated by anyone, hence Ibn ʿAshur glosses it as the Overpowering.
rows.anchor: و { العزيز } الذي لا يغلب ولا يذله أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jabbar means the subduer who compels another to undergo what He does by His act.
rows.anchor: القاهر المكره غيره على الانفعال بفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God compels creatures to their created capacities and to what He wills; humans cannot fly and quadrupeds cannot walk only on two legs.
rows.anchor: لا يستطيع مخلوق اجتياز ما حده له في خلقته فلا يستطيع الإنسان الطيران ولا يستطيع ذوات الأربع المشي على رجلين فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling a human jabbar is blameworthy because it suggests forcing other people to follow one’s desires; Ibn ʿAshur links this usage to 28:19.
rows.anchor: إذا وصف الإنسان بالجبار كان وصف ذم لأنه يشعر بأنه يحمل غيره على هواه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says he knows only jabbar and darrak as intensive forms on faʿʿal from form-IV verbs; the expected forms would be mujbir and mudrik.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : لم أسمع فعالا في أفعل إلا جبارا ودراكا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative derives al-Jabbar from repairing a break, so it means the one who sets things right.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الجبار معناه المصلح من جبر الكسر ، إذا أصلحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutakabbir means one of intense pride, greatness, and majesty.
rows.anchor: و { المتكبر } : الشديد الكبرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tafaʿʿul form usually signals affectation, but here it signals the resulting strength: an act done deliberately and carefully is more perfect; Ibn ʿAshur compares yutazallam.
rows.anchor: أصل صيغة التفعل أن تدل على التكلف لكنها استعملت هنا في لازم التكلف وهو القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAziz, al-Jabbar, and al-Mutakabbir follow al-Muhaymin to balance the earlier reassuring attributes with conquest, subjugation, and majesty that inspires awe.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الصفات في جانب التخويف كما كانت الصفات قبلها في جانب الإطماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending declares God transcendent above partners ascribed to Him; “they associate” refers to the polytheists understood from the context and repeatedly rebuked by the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: فضمير { يشركون } عائد إلى معلوم من المقام وهم المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening “He” and repetition of the clause follow the same analysis as the preceding verse; if it is a pronoun of matter, the following sentence predicates it.
rows.anchor: القول في ضمير { هو } المفتتح به وفي تكرير الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Definiteness in both parts restricts the statement to God as Creator rather than the alleged partners, refuting the divinity of what cannot create; Ibn ʿAshur cites 16:20 and 16:17.
rows.anchor: وجملة { الله الخالق } تفيد قصرا بطريق تعريف جزأي الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if “He” refers to the preceding name of God, “Allah” is its predicate and al-Khaliq is an attribute.
rows.anchor: فاسم الجلالة بعده خبر عنه و { الخالق } صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaliq is an active participle of khalq, whose basic linguistic sense is bringing a thing into being in a particular form.
rows.anchor: و { الخالق } : اسم فاعل من الخلق ، وأصل الخلق في اللغة إيجاد شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur had discussed the broader sense of creating forms in Jesus’ words about making a bird from clay, in 3:49.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم عند قوله تعالى حكاية عن عيسى عليه السلام { إني أخلق لكم من الطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalq can more narrowly mean bringing into existence what was absent; this is the dominant sense of God’s name al-Khaliq, with 50:38 as an example.
rows.anchor: ويطلق الخلق على معنى أخص من إيجاد الصور وهو إيجاد ما لم يكن موجودا

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf glosses al-Khaliq as the one who determines what He brings into being.
rows.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) : ( المقدر لما يوجده )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur explains the Kashshaf gloss by God’s acts being measured by wisdom: khalq as bringing forth from nothing, broader than forming images; he cites 7:11 on one reading.
rows.anchor: لما كانت إحداثات الله مقدرة بمقادير الحكمة عبر عن إحداثه بالخلق

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines khalq as sound proportioning, also used for originating something without prior material or a model to imitate.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : الخلق التقدير المستقيم واستعمل في إيداع الشيء من غير أصل ولا احتذاء

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi defines al-Khaliq as bringing things from nonexistence to existence with their qualities, then ranks al-Bariʾ as narrower and al-Musawwir narrower still; Ibn ʿAshur says he blends two senses.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر ابن العربي في ( عارضة الأحوذي ) على ( سنن الترمذي ) :

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali distinguishes three linked stages: measuring what will exist, bringing it into existence according to the measure, then arranging its forms beautifully; the names describe God by each stage.
rows.anchor: وقال الغزالي في ( المقصد الأسنى ) : الخالق البارىء المصور قد يظن أن هذه الأسماء مترادفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali treats the three meanings as inseparable stages distinguished by perspective, but Ibn ʿAshur says this does not fit how these names are used.
rows.anchor: فجعل المعاني متلازمة وجعل الفرق بينها بالاعتبار ، ولا أحسبه ينطبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bariʾ is the active participle of the hamzated verb baraʾa.
rows.anchor: و { البارىء } اسم فاعل من برأ مهموزا

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains al-Bariʾ as differentiating what God brings into being from one another by their varied shapes; Ibn ʿAshur finds this distinct from al-Khaliq.
rows.anchor: قال في ( الكشاف ) المميز لما يوجده بعضه من بعض بالأشكال المختلفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾanic phrase about the best and worst bariyya, plus the hadith and ʿAli’s saying, show that bariʾ is not restricted to human beings.
rows.anchor: ومن كلام علي رضي الله عنه : لا والذي فلق الحبة وبرأ النسمة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says al-bariyya means creatures.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : البريئة : الخلق

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi derives al-Bariʾ from dust and limits it to creating humankind, so al-bariyya in 98:6–7 means people.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي في ( العارضة ) : { البارىء } : خالق الناس من البرى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya explains al-Bariʾ as equivalent to al-Khaliq; the author says the lexicographer in al-Qamus does likewise.
rows.anchor: وفسره ابن عطية بمعنى الخالق . وكذلك صاحب القاموس

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali glosses al-Bariʾ as the one who brings an existent into being, an interpretation Ibn ʿAshur says does not fit usage.
rows.anchor: وفسره الغزالي بأنه الموجود المخترع ، وقد علمت أنه غير منطبق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the proposed explanations of al-Bariʾ, Ibn ʿAshur judges the Kashshaf’s differentiation by forms to be best.
rows.anchor: فأحسن تفسير له ما في ( الكشاف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Musawwir is the one who forms the visible shapes of all creatures that have visible forms.
rows.anchor: مكون الصور لجميع المخلوقات ذوات الصور المرئية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together the names portray divine origination in stages: bringing into existence, forming the human body, then granting its beautiful shape; Ibn ʿAshur links this to 82:7–8 and 3:6.
rows.anchor: فابتدىء بالخلق الذي هو الإيجاد الأصلي ثم بالبرء الذي هو تكوين جسم الإنسان ثم بالتصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the earlier attributes, these names highlight God’s wondrous creation of people and awaken gratitude, which leads into the declaration that all creation glorifies Him.
rows.anchor: ليثير داعية شكرهم على ذلك . ولذلك عقب بجملة { يسبح له ما في السماوات والأرض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur groups the closing attributes into three sets that correspond to the sūra’s subjects, while their order also follows local links such as analogy, precaution, or completion.
rows.anchor: ينقسم إلى ثلاثة أقسام ولكنها ذكرت في الآية بحسب تناسب مواقع بعضها عقب بعض من تنظير أو احتراس أو تتميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first set addresses polytheists, hostile allied Jews, and hypocrites; exclusive divinity is the basis for reflecting on the other attributes and for leaving the root of misguidance.
rows.anchor: فإن الإشراك أصل الضلالات ، والمشركون هم الذين يغرون اليهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The knowledge of the unseen counters shirk’s denial of the unseen, resurrection, judgment, revelation, and messengership; Ibn ʿAshur connects this to 8:13.
rows.anchor: فإن من أصول الشرك إنكار الغيب الذي من آثاره إنكار البعث والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names al-Malik, al-ʿAziz, al-Jabbar, and al-Mutakabbir fit the terror, disgrace, and force God brought upon Banu Nadir.
rows.anchor: لأنها تناسب ما أنزله ببني النضير من الرعب والخزي والبطشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Salam and al-Muʾmin suit the believers’ gain from Banu Nadir without deploying cavalry or camels, hardship, harm, or fighting, as 59:6 says.
rows.anchor: أي لم يتجشم المسلمون للغنى مشقة ولا أذى ولا قتالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman and al-Rahim fit God’s giving a share of the fayʾ to the weak.
rows.anchor: لمناسبتهما لإعطاء حظ في الفيء للضعفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quddus, al-Muhaymin, al-Khaliq, al-Bariʾ, and al-Musawwir concern both groups in the sūra, each of whom receives their share of these attributes.
rows.anchor: متعلق بما يشترك فيه الفريقان المذكوران في هذه السورة فيأخذ كل فريق حظه منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase sums up God’s attributes, including those just listed; it calls them names because creation names Him by them and they reach perfect truth in relation to Him.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالأسماء الصفات ، عبر عنها بالأسماء لأنه متصف بها على ألسنة خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase points to the denotations of the names, as “He displayed them” in 2:31 means that God showed the named things to the angels.
rows.anchor: والمقصود : أن له مدلولات الأسماء الحسنى كما في قوله تعالى : { ثم عرضهم على الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAshur notes the earlier command in 7:180 to call upon God by His beautiful names.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم قوله تعالى : { ولله الأسماء الحسنى فادعوه بها في سورة الأعراف . }

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about glorification is circumstantial to “to Him belong the beautiful names.”
rows.anchor: جملة { يسبح له } الخ في موضع الحال من ضمير { له الأسماء الحسنى }

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s beautiful attributes lead rational beings in the heavens and earth to exalt Him; knowledge of some names prompts every kind to glorify, intentionally or not.
rows.anchor: يضطر ما في السماوات والأرض من العقلاء على تعظيمه بالتسبيح والتنزيه عن النقائص

words: يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even an atheist or naturalist who admires the universe’s order is in reality praising the free agent, although he calls it time or nature.
rows.anchor: فالدهري أو الطبائعي إذا نوه بنظام الكائنات وأعجب بانتساقها فإنما يسبح في الواقع للفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorification may mean spoken declaration of transcendence, or may include figurative glorification by the signs things present through their state.
rows.anchor: فأما إن حمل على ما يشمل المعنيين الحقيقي والمجازي من دلالة على التنزيه ولو بلسان الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the broader figurative reading, created things’ provision and subjugation testify to God through the signs of their existence and order.
rows.anchor: ما ثبت له من صفات الخلق والإمداد والقهر تدل عليه شواهد المخلوقات وانتظام وجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He is the Mighty, the Wise” is coordinated with the preceding circumstantial clause; these attributes aptly fit the order of creation.
rows.anchor: عطف على جملة الحال وأوثر هاتان الصفتان لشدة مناسبتهما لنظام الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse closes by returning to the sūra’s opening, forming a ring around the sūra.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية رد العجز على الصدر لأن صدر السورة مماثل لآخرها

words: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِى لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits with a hasan chain from Maʿqil ibn Yasar that reciting the refuge and the last three verses morning or evening brings 70,000 angels’ prayers until the opposite time; death that day or night is martyrdom.
rows.anchor: روى الترمذي بسند حسن عن معقل بن يسار عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من قال حين يصبح ثلاث مرات

words: لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ عَلَىٰ جَبَلٍ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report passed from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud through reciters and Gabriel says placing a hand on one’s head at 59:21 brings a cure for every illness except death; Ibn ʿAshur calls it a rare serial report to Gabriel.
rows.anchor: فإني قرأت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فلما بلغت هذه الآية قال لي : ضع يدك على رأسك فإن جبريل

words: لَوْ أَنزَلْنَا هَٰذَا ٱلْقُرْءَانَ عَلَىٰ جَبَلٍ
rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Daylami reports from ʿAli and Ibn Masʿud that reciting 59:21 through the end of the sūra is a spell for headache.
rows.anchor: وأخرج الديلمي عن علي وابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال في قوله تعالى : { لو أنزلنا هذا القرآن }

words: وَإِن كَانُوا۟ مِن قَبْلُ لَفِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ مُّبِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “wa-in,” in is the lightened form of the heavy particle and does not govern its noun or predicate; kana fills the expected place, and the lām distinguishes it from negative in.
rows.anchor: و { إن } مخففة من الثقيلة وهي مهملة عن العمل في اسمها وخبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And others” cannot coordinate with “the unlettered”: its contrast requires people other than them, while the Prophet was not among non-Arabs; nor can it attach to “from them.”
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون { وآخرين } عطفا على { الأميين } ( الجمعة : 2 ) لأن آخرين يقتضي المغايرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “others” coordinates with the pronoun in “recites to them,” meaning he recites to others; prophetic recitation conveys revelation and therefore entails that he is sent to them.
rows.anchor: لأن تلاوة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم لا تكون إلا تلاوة تبليغ لما أوحي به إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parsing makes the waw comitative and “others” an object of accompaniment governed by all three verbs: reciting, purifying, and teaching.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يجعل { وآخرين } مفعولا معه . والواو للمعية ويتنازعه الأفعال الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “though they were before in clear error” is parenthetical, either between the coordinated elements or between the pronouns and the comitative object.
rows.anchor: وجملة { وإن كانوا من قبل لفي ضلال مبين } ( الجمعة : 2 ) معترضة بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akharin is a plural of akhar, “different in a respect”; contrasted here with the unlettered, it means people other than the Arabs.
rows.anchor: و { آخرين } : جمع آخر وهو المغاير

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in al-Bukhari, Muslim, and al-Tirmidhi that the Prophet identified Salman the Persian when asked who “others” were, saying that men from his people would reach faith even if it were at the Pleiades.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : كنا جلوسا عند النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فأنزلت عليه سورة الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Salman report illustrates one instance rather than exhausting “others”: the phrase covers many nations, including Persians, and Arab tribes all the more because they fall under the unlettered.
rows.anchor: والذي يلوح أنه تفسير بالجزئي على وجه المثال ليفيد أن { آخرين } صادق على أمم كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min may be partitive, with its pronoun referring back to those who were in error before: others from among them receive recitation, purification, and teaching.
rows.anchor: فلنا أن نجعل ( من ) تبعيضية كما هو المتبادر من معانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, min is connective, as in 6:159: “others” join and become part of the first community, with “from them” as a circumstantial phrase; this matches “who have not yet joined them.”
rows.anchor: ولنا أن نجعل ( من ) اتصالية كالتي في قوله تعالى : { لست منهم في شيء } ( الأنعام : 159 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “who have not yet joined them” is circumstantial; on the connective reading, later entrants into Islam become like the first Muslims.
rows.anchor: وموضع جملة { لما يلحقوا بهم } موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse hints that later peoples would Arabize themselves to understand the religion and speak the Qurʾan, a meaning Ibn ʿAshur says earlier commentators missed.
rows.anchor: وينشأ منه أيضا رمز إلى أنهم يتعربون لفهم الدين والنطق بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse foretells the call reaching non-Arab peoples—including Persians, Armenians, Kurds, Berbers, Sudanese, Romans, Turks, Tatars, Mongols, Chinese, and Indians—a Qurʾanic prediction of the unseen.
rows.anchor: وهذه بشارة غيبية بأن دعوة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستبلغ أمما ليسوا من العرب وهم فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that the Prophet’s message is universal and addressed to all nations.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على عموم رسالة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لجميع الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Negative lamma keeps negation in force up to the time of speaking and suggests the awaited event will occur; Ibn ʿAshur cites 49:14 and al-Kashshaf’s gloss.
rows.anchor: والنفي ب ( لما ) يقتضي أن المنفي بها مستمر الانتفاء إلى زمن التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At revelation these other peoples had not entered Islam or joined the Arabs who had; the wording predicts their joining in later times.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن آخرين هم في وقت نزول هذه الآية لم يدخلوا في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky described here as split may be different from, or identical with, the sky described as a rose-like form in 55:37.
rows.anchor: ثم يحتمل أنه غير الذي في قوله تعالى : { فإذا انشقت السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahiya literally means weak and dispersed; metaphorically it describes ease and lack of resistance, as in “his resolve slackened” and the proverb about the spider’s web.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة { واهية } ضعيفة ومتفرقة ، ويستعار الوهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That day” marks a new weakness after the sky’s former solidity, called ratq elsewhere; its splitting is fatq, leaving it open and traversable.
rows.anchor: أن الوهي طرا عليها بعد أن كانت صلبة بتماسك أجزائها وهو المعبر عنه في القرآن بالرتق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy is close in meaning to wahn, but is more often used of inanimate things and wahn of people.
rows.anchor: والوهي : قريب من الوهن ، والأكثر أن الوهي يوصف به الأشياء غير العاقلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s rupture lets angels travel up and down through it, unlike its former state; Ibn ʿAshur again links this to 55:37.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن الملائكة يترددون إليها صعودا ونزولا خلافا لحالها من قبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The angels are at its edges” is a circumstantial clause describing the pronoun in “it will be weak.”
rows.anchor: وجملة { والملك على أرجائها ، } حال من ضمير { فهي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malak is singular for an angel; here its definite form is generic and collective, meaning a group or all angels, with a singular form making totality more explicit.
rows.anchor: و { الملك } : أصله الواحد من الملائكة ، وتعريفه هنا تعريف الجنس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas observes that the singular “book” is more explicit than “books” in indicating the whole, as an analogy for the collective singular.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال ابن عباس : الكتاب أكثر من الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arjaʾ means sides or edges in the Hudhayl dialect; its singular is the shortened raja, whose alif derives from waw.
rows.anchor: والأرجاء : النواحي بلغة هذيل ، واحدها رجا مقصورا وألفه منقلبة عن الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in arjaʾiha refers to the sky.
rows.anchor: وضمير { أرجائها } عائد إلى { السماء .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels work in the sky’s regions, bringing the people of Paradise down to Paradise and driving the people of Hell toward the Fire.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : أن الملائكة يعملون في نواحي السماء ينفذون إنزال أهل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Throne is a name for what encompasses the heavens and is greater than the heavens.
rows.anchor: وعرش الرب : اسم لما يحيط بالسماوات وهو أعظم من السماوات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported view takes the eight bearers of the Throne as eight individual angels.
rows.anchor: فقيل : ثمانية شخوص

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported view takes the eight bearers as eight rows of angels.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ثمانية صفوف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands eight tenths of the angels, approximately eighty angels, as the bearers.
rows.anchor: وقيل ثمانية أعشار ، أي نحو ثمانين من مجموع عدد الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The source mentions other interpretations of the eight bearers without specifying them.
rows.anchor: وقيل غير ذلك ، وهذا من أحوال الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The details are unseen and not needed; the verse’s purpose is to represent God’s greatness in a way people can grasp.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أحوال الغيب التي لا يتعلق الغرض بتفصيلها ، إذ المقصود من الآية تمثيل عظمة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond admonition, the passage may symbolically teach the Prophet something of those unseen states while leaving their full detail unopened for us.
rows.anchor: ولعل المقصود بالإشارة إلى ما زاد على الموعظة ، هو تعليم الله نبيئه شيئا من تلك الأحوال بطريقة رمزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels are mentioned collectively to make the transition to news of the Throne less abrupt.
rows.anchor: وكأن الداعي إلى ذكرهم إجمالا هو الانتقال إلى الأخبار عن عرش الله لئلا يكون ذكره اقتضابا

rows.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits from al-ʿAbbas a Prophetic report about distances between the heavens; Tirmidhi uses symbolic descriptions of the Throne’s bearers to interpret this verse.
rows.anchor: وروى الترمذي عن العباس بن عبد المطلب عن النبي حديثا ذكر فيه أبعاد ما بين السماوات

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari says that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmayra is not known to have heard from al-Ahnaf ibn Qays, a narrator in al-Tirmidhi’s report.
rows.anchor: قال البخاري : لا نعلم له سماعا عن الأحنف .

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi dismisses other reports as fabrications from the People of the Book or poetry of Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt; it is not established that the Prophet recited and approved the poem.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي فيها : إنها متلفقات من أهل الكتاب أو من شعر لأمية بن أبي الصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “above them” refers to the angels.
rows.anchor: وضمير فوقهم } يعود إلى { الملك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Above them” with “bear the Throne” reinforces the height already implied by bearing it, like the added restrictions in 6:38.
rows.anchor: ويتعلق { فوقهم } ب { يحمل عرش ربك } وهو تأكيد لما دل عليه يحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address in the Throne-bearing clause is directed to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للنبيء صلى الله عليه وسلم وإضافة عرش إلى الله إضافة تشريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The possessive is an honorific, like God’s “House” for the Kaʿba in 22:26; God is beyond sitting on the Throne or dwelling in a house.
rows.anchor: والله منزه عن الجلوس على العرش وعن السكنى في بيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You will be presented” addresses all people, as the context and the following details show.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في قوله : { تعرضون } لجميع الناس بقرينة المقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿArḍ originally means passing things before someone for inspection, like merchandise before a buyer or troops before a commander; here it alludes to reckoning, while the literal sense may also apply.
rows.anchor: والعرض : أصله إمرار الأشياء على من يريد التأمل منها مثل عرض السلعة على المشتري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No hidden thing is concealed from God or His angels.
rows.anchor: لا تخفى على الله ولا على ملائكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine khafiya may describe an implicit feminine act, or a soul/person: no one can hide from the accounting.
rows.anchor: وتأنيث { خافية } لأنه وصف لموصوف مؤنث يقدر بالفعلة من أفعال العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At judgment no one is hidden and no confusion remains between believer and unbeliever or virtuous and wicked.
rows.anchor: ولا يلتبس كافر بمؤمن ، ولا بار بفاجر .
